title: Define clear time‑based validation splits before modeling
when_to_use: When the task asks to predict future outcomes or trends using historical data.
experience:
- Before any feature engineering, explicitly define the **training, validation, and future (test) periods** using calendar dates or relative windows.
- Ensure the split respects chronological order and **prevents leakage** (e.g., future data must not influence past features).
- **Count the number of entities** (e.g., accounts, visitors) available in each window and report them to verify data sufficiency.
- If data is sparse, consider alternative entity levels (e.g., visitor‑ instead of account‑level) or extend windows, but document the trade‑off.
- **Store the split definitions** as parameters in a config table so they can be easily adjusted or audited later.
checklist: Define exact date ranges for training/validation/test windows
Verify entity counts per window meet minimum sample size
Ensure no future information leaks into training features
Document the split logic and any deviations
common_failure_prevented: Building a predictive model with data‑leakage from lifetime aggregates that leads to unrealistic accuracy.

title: Construct and evaluate the target variable with business logic
when_to_use: When the task requires identifying a high‑value segment or predicting a binary outcome without a predefined label.
experience:
- **Define the target variable explicitly** using business‑relevant metrics (e.g., top‑X% of engagement, revenue, or growth).
- If multiple indicators exist, **combine them into a composite label** (e.g., high‑value = high usage AND high frequency) and justify the logic.
- **Calculate the label separately for each time window** (e.g., training vs. future) to avoid look‑ahead bias.
- **Analyze label distribution** across windows; if imbalanced, discuss implications for modeling and consider oversampling or threshold adjustments.
- **Validate label stability** by checking how many entities change status across windows; high volatility may indicate a noisy target.
checklist: Document the exact formula/computation for the target variable
Compute label statistics (count, proportion) per window
Check for label drift across time periods
If imbalanced, decide on mitigation strategy
common_failure_prevented: Using a static, poorly‑defined high‑value label that does not reflect temporal dynamics, leading to uninterpretable model performance.

title: Report model performance on a hold‑out test set with required metrics
when_to_use: When the task requires achieving a specific performance threshold (e.g., >85% accuracy) or comparing models.
experience:
- **Hold out a test set chronologically** (or via cross‑validation) that was never used during model development.
- **Compute all required metrics** (accuracy, precision, recall, F1, etc.) **on the test set only** and report them in a clear table.
- If a performance threshold is given (e.g., precision ≥0.85), **tune the decision threshold** on the validation set to meet it, then verify on the test set.
- **Compare against the baseline/model** explicitly using the same test set; highlight differences in key metrics, not just overall accuracy.
- **Provide a confusion matrix** or top‑K identification rate to give a fuller picture of model strengths and weaknesses.
checklist: Evaluate final model on an untouched test set
Report precision, recall, F1, and accuracy
Adjust decision threshold to meet any specified target
Compare new model vs. baseline on the same test data
common_failure_prevented: Reporting inflated performance from training data and failing to verify that the model meets the business requirement on unseen data.
